title: FLA binary read+write drops non-solid stroke styles: styleParam1/styleParam2 skipped on import, written as 0 — dashed/dotted/ragged/stippled/hatched strokes don't survive despite full model+SWF support
description: The model has first-class stroke styles (engine/types.ts:172-228 StrokeStyle: dashed{dashLength,gapLength}/dotted{dotSpacing}/ragged/stippled/hatched via Stroke.style, tasks 0037+1069 added UI/render/SWF emit), but the FLA binary codec ignores them on BOTH paths: (a) READ — flash8-binary.ts readLineStyle:1504-1538 does r.skip(4) over styleParam1+styleParam2 ('dash/dot/ragged parameters' per its own comment), so a real Flash 8 FLA authored with a dashed/dotted/ragged/stippled/hatched stroke imports as a plain solid stroke with no warning; Fla8Stroke has no style field at all. (b) WRITE — write/timeline-write.ts writeLineStyle:607-626 hardcodes w.u32(0) for both params, so a dash-styled stroke authored in dash and saved as real FLA silently reverts to solid on reopen. docs/21 sec 12.2 documents the fields ('u16 styleParam1; u16 styleParam2 — dash, dot, ragged, stipple, or hatch parameters; low three bits select the style; +0x8000 selects sharp corners from MX'), and JPEXS flacomdoc (clone locally per CLAUDE.md) has the byte-verified writer for each style's parameter packing. Why it matters: full-fidelity FLA round-trip is the workstream contract; this is a silent authored-data loss in both directions with the model already able to carry it. Fix: decode styleParam1/2 into Fla8Stroke.style (map the low-3-bit selector + per-style parameter fields per flacomdoc LineStyle writers), thread through strokeFromFla8 (flash8-import.ts:164-189) to Stroke.style, and emit the inverse in writeLineStyle. Acceptance: round-trip test per style type (dashed/dotted/ragged/stippled/hatched with non-default parameters) through saveRealFla -> tryLoadRealFla asserting Stroke.style deep-equals; plus a decode-only test pinning the selector bits against the flacomdoc-documented encoding. Note: parameter-field packing beyond the 3 selector bits is unverified against a real fixture — mark any guessed sub-field layout in comments and prefer flacomdoc's writer as the source.
